name: merc
comment: A minimal TextMate grammar covering keywords/comments/operators/numbers only — deliberately not a full parser (that's what merc-lsp's semantic tokens are for; see semantic_tokens.rs's module docs). This is purely the coloring fallback for clients/moments a TextMate grammar can reach that the LSP can't: before the language server has started, on a document that fails to parse, or in a client with no semantic tokens support at all. Shared by the merc/merc-pbes/merc-pres language contributions in package.json — merc, PBES, and PRES source share one lexical layer (comments, operators, identifiers, numbers) and almost all of the same keyword set; PBES/PRES only add a handful of their own ('pbes', 'pres', 'mu', 'nu').

comments.comment: merc's only comment syntax: '%' to end of line, no escape and no block form.
comments.name: comment.line.percentage.merc

patterns.comment: Structural/block-introducing keywords — shared by process specifications, PBES, and PRES. Word-bounded so e.g. 'sortable' isn't matched.
patterns.name: keyword.control.merc

patterns.comment: Reserved literal/value keywords — see merc_syntax's `keywords_are_not_prefix_of_identifiers` test for why these (unlike the rest of this file) are true reserved words, not just conventionally-unclaimed identifiers.
patterns.name: constant.language.merc

constants.comment: The built-in system sorts (Bool, Nat, Int, ...) get the same scope a user `sort` declaration's name would, distinguished by the LSP's own semantic tokens (a 'defaultLibrary' modifier) rather than here — a TextMate grammar has no notion of what's actually declared.
constants.name: support.type.merc
